cands.name: Josie Tomkow
cands.bio: Republican former state representative (HD 39 from 2018, HD 51 from 2022, left the House in 2026). Seventh-generation Floridian and third-generation cattle rancher; University of Florida graduate; chaired the House Health & Human Services Committee. Lost the March 2026 SD 14 special election to Brian Nathan by about 0.5 point.
cands.local_ties: Her campaign site says she lives in South Tampa with her husband, Thomas. Born in Tampa (Wikipedia). Earlier represented Polk/Hillsborough House districts.

record.text: Florida House 2018-2026: HD 39, then HD 51; resigned to run for SD 14 (Wikipedia gives 2025 and March 17, 2026 as exit dates; exact date unverified).

Creative Loafing notes she voted for SB 256 (2023, public-sector union restrictions), did not vote on the final version of HB 433 (2024, preempts local workplace rules) and voted yes on a 2026 public-sector union recertification law.

controversies.text: 2020 Ledger report raised questions whether she met the House residency requirement, after a review of 2018 traffic citations listing a Dade City address.

endorsements.text: Campaign site lists Rep. Laurel Lee, Hillsborough Commissioner Christine Miller, and Sheriffs Chad Chronister, Grady Judd, Chris Nocco and Bob Gualtieri.
Florida Chamber of Commerce; Florida Medical Association; Tampa, Suncoast and West Central PBAs; Hillsborough and Tampa firefighters (per her site).

cands.gaps: No money/donor reporting found. Owner-source search not run (search budget exhausted). Wikipedia claims about a Florida Rising endorsement for her were not corroborated and are left out.

votes.what: The 2025-26 General Appropriations Act (state budget), final vote.
Immigration enforcement bill from the 2025 special session: state cooperation with federal immigration enforcement.
Post-hurricane emergency management bill that also limits local governments' ability to adopt stricter development rules after storms.
Online Protections for Minors: restricts social media accounts for minors.
Interests of foreign countries: restricts land purchases near military sites and critical infrastructure by people from China and other 'countries of concern'.
Education: expands school voucher eligibility to all Florida K-12 students.
Heartbeat Protection Act: bans most abortions after six weeks of pregnancy.
Public Safety: lets most adults carry a concealed firearm without a permit (permitless carry).
Property Insurance: creates the Florida Optional Reinsurance Assistance program (FORA) for insurers.
Building Safety (condo safety response after Surfside).

cands.name: Brian Nathan
cands.bio: Democratic state senator for SD 14 since winning the March 24, 2026 special election. Navy veteran (cryptology specialist, 2003-2008); University of Tampa B.A. (sociology and philosophy); IBEW Local 915 electrician/foreman and organizer; Florida AFL-CIO Working Families Lobby Corps member.
cands.local_ties: Campaign site says he and his wife chose Tampa as home after leaving the Navy in 2008; mailing address is a PO Box. SD 14 is western Hillsborough County.

record.text: Won the March 24, 2026 special election 50.26% (40,245) to 49.74% (39,836) over Josie Tomkow; November is a rematch.
Platform: good-paying jobs with worker protections, housing affordability, holding insurance and utility companies accountable, fully funding schools, health care access.

money_notes.text: Tampa Bay Times (Oct 14, 2026) covers Republican 'leftist' attacks on him; the URL references the Republican Senatorial Campaign Committee. Only the headline and subhead were readable, so the money details are unverified.

controversies.text: A Republican ad for Tomkow used a photo of Nathan at a May Day event and called him a socialist; Creative Loafing says the event was a labor rally also organized by other groups.

endorsements.text: Creative Loafing Tampa Bay recommends Nathan (2026 voting guide).

Campaign site lists: AFSCME Florida, Florida AFL-CIO, IBEW Local 915, SEIU, Florida Education Association, Florida Nurses Association, Equality Florida Action PAC, Florida Rising, VoteVets; Rep. Kathy Castor; Sen.-elect Fentrice Driskell. West Central Florida Labor Council also endorsed.

cands.gaps: No donor or committee spending figures verified (Florida Politics and Tampa Bay Times article bodies unreadable). Owner-source search not run (search budget exhausted).
